domain.text: Security: gateway role authorization from credential identity

impressions.text: The delivery used codexbal/gpt-6.1-sol to implement credential-derived gateway authority and was merged after a dev integration round.
The worker reported broad regression coverage, strict identity-boundary tests, and successful required checks; the orchestrator also reported live smoke checks of role behavior.

Review caught successive CI authentication mismatches, including the Actions viewer’s actual type, and an unconfigured Claude worker-token requirement; the worker requested authenticated guidance rather than weakening boundaries speculatively.
The orchestrator authorized a narrow CI learning-check exception and directed removal of Claude model families from the repository’s own configuration pending an owner-provisioned token.
The worker reported isolating Vitest state after a shared-user journal lock was encountered; it left the existing real-home test directory untouched because ownership was uncertain.

roundCauses.text: CI learning/changelog validation initially failed because the Actions credential’s GraphQL viewer did not match the configured identity pin; the reported viewer type was User rather than Bot.
After the learning/changelog gate passed, the self-check failed because the repository lacked the required worker-token configuration for its Claude model families.
A later review round followed merges to dev and required integration of overlapping changes across five conflicted files.

findings.text: Gateway authority is derived from the configured token’s pinned viewer identity; VMETHOD_ROLE can narrow but not elevate authority.
The system identity exception is limited to learning-check operations under GitHub Actions, with other system operations still refused.
The orchestrator reported that the merged build refuses an orchestrator token in worker task context while permitting orchestrator commands and worker narrowing without a task.
